items.prompt: What is the SI unit of frequency?

options.label: Watt
Metre
Decibel
Hertz

rubric: Frequency is measured in hertz (cycles per second).
Decibel is for sound level and metre is for wavelength.

items.prompt: Which equation links wave speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ?

options.label: v = f × λ
v = f / λ
v = λ / f
v = f + λ

rubric: Wave speed equals frequency times wavelength.
Distractors invert or misuse the relationship.

items.prompt: What is the term for the maximum displacement of a wave from its equilibrium position?

options.label: Wavelength
Amplitude
Phase
Period

rubric: Amplitude is the maximum displacement from equilibrium.
Wavelength is a distance between repeating points, not displacement.

items.prompt: What does the law of reflection state?

options.label: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
The reflected ray always leaves the surface at 90 degrees
The ray bends toward the normal when it meets the surface
The angle of incidence is twice the angle of reflection

rubric: Incident and reflected angles are equal, measured from the normal.
The last option confuses reflection with refraction.

items.prompt: Which type of wave is sound in air?

options.label: Transverse wave
Electromagnetic wave
Longitudinal wave
Surface wave

rubric: Sound in air is a longitudinal pressure wave.
Learners often confuse it with transverse waves such as light.

items.prompt: Which of the following are parts of the electromagnetic spectrum? Select all that apply.

options.label: Ultraviolet
Infrared
Ultrasound
Microwaves
Sound

rubric: Microwaves, UV and infrared are electromagnetic waves.
Ultrasound and sound are mechanical waves, not electromagnetic.

items.prompt: A student watches a ripple tank. A dipper bobs up and down 5 times each second, creating ripples. The student is asked to name the quantity that describes 5 bobs per second. Which term is correct?

options.label: Wave speed
Wavelength
Frequency
Amplitude

rubric: Number of oscillations per second is frequency.
Wave speed is distance per time, not oscillations per time.

items.prompt: What happens to the wavelength of a wave of fixed speed if its frequency doubles?

options.label: It stays the same
It halves
It quadruples
It doubles

rubric: Since v = fλ with v fixed, λ is inversely proportional to f.
Doubling is the direct-proportion error.

items.prompt: Light travels from air into glass. What happens to its speed and frequency?

options.label: Speed stays the same; frequency decreases
Speed increases; frequency stays the same
Speed decreases; frequency stays the same
Speed decreases; frequency increases

rubric: Frequency is set by the source; speed drops in glass.
Distractors wrongly change the frequency.

items.prompt: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?

options.label: It changes into light waves once no air is present
It moves too slowly to get across empty space
It needs a medium to pass vibrations along
Empty space absorbs sound energy completely

rubric: Sound is a mechanical wave needing particles to vibrate.
Other options invent absorption or conversion effects.

items.prompt: A converging lens brings parallel rays to a point. How is that image-forming point described?

options.label: The normal
The optical axis
The centre of curvature
The focal point

rubric: Parallel rays converge at the focal point of a converging lens.
The normal is a line perpendicular to a surface, not a convergence point.

items.prompt: Two waves meet and their crests line up with each other. What is this effect called?

options.label: Diffraction
Constructive interference
Total internal reflection
Destructive interference

rubric: Crests aligning add to a larger amplitude.
Destructive interference occurs when crest meets trough.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe diffraction of waves through a gap? Select all that apply.

options.label: It is the spreading of waves as they pass through a gap
It is the bouncing of waves back from a barrier
It only happens to light, not to sound
It is most noticeable when the gap is similar in size to the wavelength

rubric: Diffraction is spreading, strongest when gap size is near wavelength.
It happens for all waves; bouncing back is reflection.

items.prompt: A student shines a ray of light from air into a water tank at an angle. The ray bends toward the normal as it enters the water. What best explains this bending?

options.label: Light slows down in water, changing its direction
Light speeds up in water, changing its direction
The frequency of light increases in water, bending it
Water absorbs part of the light, tilting the ray

rubric: Refraction toward the normal occurs when light slows in the denser medium.
Speeding up would bend the ray away from the normal.

items.prompt: A wave travels along a rope at a fixed speed. If the frequency of the source is doubled while the rope stays the same, what happens to the wavelength?

options.label: It is doubled
It stays the same
It is halved
It is quadrupled

rubric: Speed is fixed by the medium, so v = f x wavelength means doubling f halves the wavelength.
Distractors treat wavelength as independent of frequency or as proportional to it.

items.prompt: Why can sound from a bell not travel through a vacuum?

options.label: Sound needs air specifically, and no other material works
A vacuum reflects all sound waves back to the source
Sound is carried by vibrating particles, and a vacuum has none
Sound is too slow to cross empty space before it fades

rubric: Sound is a mechanical wave that needs a medium of particles to pass on compressions.
Distractors suggest it only needs air or is reflected, which misses the need for a medium.

items.prompt: Light passes from air into glass. Which quantity does NOT change?

options.label: Frequency
Wavelength
Direction at an angled boundary
Speed

rubric: Frequency is set by the source and stays the same across a boundary.
Speed and wavelength both decrease in glass; learners often think wavelength stays fixed.

items.prompt: Two identical waves meet at a point and cancel completely. What must be true about their path difference?

options.label: It is zero
It is equal to the amplitude of the waves
It is an odd multiple of half a wavelength
It is a whole number of wavelengths

rubric: Waves arriving in antiphase cancel, which needs a path difference of (n + 1/2) wavelengths.
Whole numbers of wavelengths or zero give constructive interference.

items.prompt: A water wave passes through a gap in a harbour wall. When does it spread out (diffract) the most?

options.label: When the wave travels very fast
When the gap is close to one wavelength
When the wave has a very large amplitude
When the gap is much wider than the wavelength

rubric: Diffraction is strongest when gap width is comparable to wavelength.
Learners wrongly link spreading to a wide gap, big amplitude or high speed.

items.prompt: Which statements correctly describe transverse waves? Select all that apply.

options.label: Particles of the medium oscillate perpendicular to the direction of travel
Transverse waves can be polarised
Sound in air is a transverse wave
Transverse waves can only travel through a material medium

items.prompt: A student stands in a corridor just around a corner from an open classroom door. She can hear the teacher clearly but cannot see the teacher. Which explanation is best?

options.label: Sound travels faster than light, so it reaches her before light can
Sound is a transverse wave, so it can turn corners that light cannot
Light is absorbed by the corridor walls, whereas sound is reflected by them and so reaches her
Sound has a much longer wavelength than light, so it diffracts round the door edge more

rubric: Sound wavelengths (about metres) are comparable to a doorway, so diffraction is large; light wavelengths are tiny.
Distractors use wrong speed comparisons or mislabel sound as transverse.

items.prompt: A note has frequency 440 Hz and wavelength 0.78 m in air. What is the speed of the sound?
rubric: v = f x wavelength = 440 x 0.78, about 343 m/s.
Distractors come from dividing instead of multiplying or from halving.

items.prompt: A light ray hits an air-glass boundary at 30 degrees to the normal. The glass has refractive index 1.5. What is the angle of refraction, to the nearest 0.5 degree?

options.label: 45 degrees
30 degrees
19.5 degrees
48.5 degrees

rubric: sin(r) = sin(30)/1.5 = 0.333, so r is about 19.5 degrees.
48.5 degrees comes from multiplying by 1.5 instead of dividing.

items.prompt: An object is 30 cm from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Using 1/f = 1/u + 1/v, how far from the lens is the image?

options.label: 20 cm
15 cm
30 cm
7.5 cm

rubric: 7.5 cm comes from inverting the sum incorrectly; the others are guesses.

items.prompt: A mass on a spring has period T = 2 x pi x sqrt(m/k). The mass is changed to four times its original value on the same spring. What is the new period?

options.label: 2T
4T

rubric: Period scales with sqrt(m), so four times the mass doubles the period.
4T ignores the square root; the smaller values invert the relationship.

items.prompt: A person stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is the person from their own image?

options.label: 4 m
2 m
8 m
1 m

rubric: The image is 2 m behind the mirror, so the separation is 2 + 2 = 4 m.
2 m ignores the distance behind the mirror.

items.prompt: In a double-slit experiment, fringe spacing is y = (wavelength x L) / d. Which changes would make the fringes spread farther apart? Select all that apply.

options.label: Use red light instead of blue light
Move the screen farther from the slits
Move the two slits farther apart
Make the light source brighter

rubric: Longer wavelength and larger L increase y; red has a longer wavelength than blue.
Increasing slit separation d reduces spacing, and brightness does not affect it.

items.prompt: A hiker shouts toward a cliff and hears the echo 2.0 s later. The speed of sound in the air is 340 m/s. Treating the sound as travelling straight to the cliff and back, how far away is the cliff?
rubric: Total distance = 340 x 2.0 = 680 m, which is there and back, so the cliff is 340 m away.
680 m forgets the round trip; 170 m and 1360 m misuse the time.

items.prompt: A string has tension 100 N and mass per unit length 0.010 kg/m. It vibrates at 250 Hz. What is the wavelength of the wave on the string?
rubric: Wave speed is sqrt(T/mu) = 100 m/s, so wavelength = v/f = 0.40 m.
Distractors come from forgetting the square root or inverting v/f.

items.prompt: A pipe closed at one end and open at the other is 0.85 m long. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m/s, what is its fundamental frequency?

options.label: 100 Hz
200 Hz
50 Hz
400 Hz

rubric: A closed pipe has a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, so L = lambda/4 and f = v/4L = 100 Hz.
200 Hz treats the pipe as open at both ends.

items.prompt: A light ray in air strikes a flat glass surface (n = 1.5) at an angle of incidence of 30° to the normal. What is the angle of refraction in the glass?
rubric: Snell's law gives sin(theta) = sin(30°)/1.5 = 0.333, so theta is about 19.5°.
48.6° results from multiplying by n instead of dividing.

items.prompt: A converging lens has focal length 10 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. At what distance from the lens does the image form?

options.label: 7.5 cm
15 cm
20 cm
40 cm

rubric: 7.5 cm and 40 cm come from adding or mishandling the reciprocals.

items.prompt: In a double-slit experiment the slit separation is 0.20 mm, the screen is 2.0 m away, and the wavelength is 600 nm. What is the spacing between adjacent bright fringes?

options.label: 0.6 mm
6 mm
60 mm
12 mm

rubric: Fringe spacing = lambda L / d = (600e-9)(2.0)/(2.0e-4) = 6 mm.
Other values come from power-of-ten slips or doubling the result.

items.prompt: Light passes from air into water (n = 1.33) at an oblique angle of incidence. Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.label: The ray bends toward the normal
Its frequency stays the same
Its speed is lower than in air
Its wavelength becomes longer because the light slows down

rubric: Frequency is set by the source and is unchanged; speed and wavelength drop by a factor of n, and the ray bends toward the normal.
The last option confuses frequency with wavelength.

items.prompt: An ambulance siren emits 700 Hz. The ambulance drives straight toward a stationary pedestrian at 30 m/s. The speed of sound is 340 m/s. What frequency does the pedestrian hear?

options.label: 762 Hz
700 Hz
643 Hz
768 Hz

rubric: For a moving source approaching, f' = f v/(v - vs) = 700(340/310), about 768 Hz.
643 Hz is the receding case; 762 Hz uses v + vs inverted in the wrong place.

items.prompt: A tuning fork of unknown frequency is sounded with a 440 Hz reference fork and produces 4 beats per second. Wax is added to the unknown fork, lowering its frequency slightly, and the beat rate rises to 6 per second. What was the unknown fork's original frequency?

options.label: 434 Hz
436 Hz
444 Hz
446 Hz

rubric: Lowering the frequency increased the beat rate, so the fork must have been below 440 Hz: 436 Hz.
If it had been 444 Hz, lowering it would have reduced the beat rate.

items.prompt: In a double-slit experiment with slits of finite width, the bright fringes fade gradually and some vanish at large angles. What best explains this?

options.label: Energy spreads over more fringes at large angles, so each fringe carries less power than the last one
Each slit's single-slit diffraction pattern forms an intensity envelope that modulates the interference fringes
Light from the two slits gradually loses spatial coherence at larger angles, so the fringe contrast falls to zero
The path difference grows at large angles, so fringes from neighbouring orders overlap and cancel one another out

rubric: The total pattern is the interference term multiplied by the single-slit diffraction envelope, so fringes at envelope minima vanish.
Coherence loss and overlap explanations do not predict missing fringes at specific angles.

items.prompt: A soap film in air looks black where it is much thinner than the wavelength of light. Why?

options.label: Only the front-surface reflection adds a half-cycle phase shift, so the two reflections cancel almost exactly
The film is too thin to reflect any light, so nothing returns to the eye at those points
The path difference there is one full wavelength, so the two reflected waves cancel each other
Both reflections add a half-cycle phase shift, so the reflected waves cancel and the film transmits everything

rubric: Front reflection (air to soap) shifts phase by half a cycle, back reflection does not; with negligible path difference they cancel.
If both reflections shifted phase, thin film would be bright, not dark.

items.prompt: A guitarist raises string tension by 21% and predicts the 220 Hz fundamental becomes about 266 Hz. What is the flaw in this prediction, and what is the better value?

options.label: Frequency scales inversely with tension, so it falls by about 17% to about 182 Hz
Frequency scales with the square root of tension, so it rises about 10% to about 242 Hz
Frequency scales as the square of tension, so it rises by about 46% to about 321 Hz
Frequency is independent of tension and set only by length, so it stays at 220 Hz

rubric: Fundamental frequency is proportional to sqrt(T), so 220 x sqrt(1.21) = 242 Hz.
The student treated frequency as directly proportional to tension.

items.prompt: A light ray inside glass (n = 1.50) meets a glass-water boundary (water n = 1.33) at 60° incidence. A student expects total internal reflection because 60° exceeds the glass-air critical angle of 41.8°. What actually happens?

options.label: Part of the beam refracts into the water, because 60° is below the 62.5° critical angle for this pair
The beam is totally reflected, because light always reflects fully going from higher to lower index
The beam is totally reflected, because 60° exceeds the critical angle of 41.8° for this boundary
The beam passes straight through undeviated, because the two refractive indices are almost equal

rubric: The critical angle for glass-water is arcsin(1.33/1.50), about 62.5°, so 60° is below it and light is transmitted partly.
The student applied the glass-air critical angle to a different boundary.

items.prompt: You hear a conversation through an open door from around a corner but cannot see the speakers. Which statements help explain this? Select all that apply.

options.label: Visible light wavelengths (about 500 nm) are far smaller than the door, so its diffraction is negligible
Light is absorbed by the wall while sound is not, so only sound gets through
Lower-pitched components bend more, so the voices sound deeper around the corner
Sound wavelengths (tens of cm to metres) are comparable to the door width, so sound diffracts strongly
Sound travels faster than light in air, so it can bend around the corner

rubric: Diffraction depends on wavelength relative to opening size; long sound wavelengths bend, especially low pitches, while light barely does.
Speed and absorption claims do not explain the bending.

items.prompt: A student places a candle 15 cm from a converging lens of focal length 20 cm and slides a screen along the bench but never finds a sharp image. What explains this?

options.label: The object sits exactly at the focal point, so the emerging rays are parallel and no image forms
The image is real and forms 60 cm beyond the lens, but it is magnified so much that the screen cannot capture it
The object is inside the focal length, so the image is virtual and cannot land on a screen
A converging lens only forms images of distant objects, so a nearby candle cannot be imaged

rubric: With u = 15 cm < f = 20 cm, 1/v = 1/20 - 1/15 gives v = -60 cm: a virtual image on the object's side.
The focal-point option misreads 15 cm as equal to f.

items.prompt: A string fixed at both ends vibrates in its third harmonic at 300 Hz. The tension is then quadrupled, with length and mass per unit length unchanged. What is the frequency of the new fundamental?

options.label: 400 Hz
100 Hz
141 Hz
200 Hz

rubric: Original fundamental is 100 Hz; wave speed scales as the square root of tension, so quadrupling tension doubles it to 200 Hz.
Distractors: 100 Hz ignores the tension change, 400 Hz treats speed as proportional to tension, and 141 Hz uses a square-root factor of 2 on frequency.

items.prompt: A soap film (n = 1.33) in air becomes far thinner than a wavelength of visible light, and it looks black in reflected white light. What best explains this?

options.label: Both surfaces reflect with a half-cycle phase shift, so the two reflected waves cancel despite the thin film
The front-surface reflection gains a half-cycle phase shift and the back one does not, so the waves cancel
The film is too thin to reflect any light, because reflection needs a thickness of several wavelengths
The extra path inside the film is one full wavelength for every color, so all colors cancel by interference

rubric: Only the air-to-film reflection inverts; with negligible path difference the two reflections are half a cycle apart and cancel.
Distractors assume both reflections invert, deny reflection from thin layers, or invoke a path difference that cannot be one wavelength for all colors.

items.prompt: A double-slit setup in air shows fringes with spacing s on a screen. The whole setup, including the screen, is submerged in water (n = 1.33) with the same laser. What happens to the fringe spacing?

options.label: It is unchanged, since the frequency of the light is the same in air and in water
It falls to about 56% of s, since both the wavelength and the slit separation scale by 1/n
It falls to about 75% of s, since the wavelength shrinks by n at fixed frequency
It rises by about 33%, since light slows down in water and so spreads further past the slits

rubric: Fringe spacing is proportional to wavelength, and wavelength in water is the air value divided by n, giving about 0.75 s.
Distractors confuse speed with spreading, treat constant frequency as constant spacing, or wrongly scale the slit separation as well.

items.prompt: A siren emits 500 Hz in still air (sound speed 340 m/s). In case A the siren moves at 34 m/s toward a stationary listener. In case B the listener moves at 34 m/s toward the stationary siren. Which comparison is correct?

options.label: Both give 550 Hz, since only the relative speed between source and listener matters for waves in a medium
A gives about 556 Hz and B about 550 Hz, since a moving source also compresses the wavelength in the air itself
A gives about 550 Hz and B about 556 Hz, since the air is at rest relative to the listener in case A
B gives about 556 Hz and A about 550 Hz, since a moving listener meets wave crests at a faster rate than a moving source does

rubric: Source motion: f = 500*340/306 = about 556 Hz; observer motion: f = 500*374/340 = 550 Hz. The medium makes the cases asymmetric.
Distractors swap the results or assume the symmetric relativistic-style rule, which does not hold for sound.

items.prompt: A grating has 500 lines/mm and is lit with white light (400 to 700 nm). A third-order violet line (400 nm) appears at a certain angle. What wavelength from the second-order spectrum appears at the same angle?

options.label: 560 nm
600 nm
800 nm
267 nm

rubric: Grating equation d sin(theta) = m*lambda gives 3*400 = 2*lambda, so lambda = 600 nm.
Distractors use wrong ratios of orders (800 nm), invert the ratio (267 nm), or guess a value in the visible range.

items.prompt: Light travels inside glass (n = 1.50) and meets a glass-water boundary (water n = 1.33). Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.label: Beyond the critical angle an evanescent field exists in the water but carries no net energy away
Total internal reflection occurs for incidence angles above about 62 degrees
The critical angle is given by arcsin(1.50/1.33)
Total internal reflection can occur for light going from water into glass at large incidence angles

rubric: Critical angle is arcsin(1.33/1.50), about 62.5 degrees; past it the transmitted field is evanescent with no average power flow.
Distractors reverse the direction (TIR needs light going into the lower index) or invert the ratio, which exceeds 1 and is undefined.

items.prompt: Two speakers 2.0 m apart emit the same in-phase 686 Hz tone (speed of sound 343 m/s). A listener stands at a point 3.00 m from one speaker and 3.75 m from the other. What does the listener hear, and why?

options.label: A loud spot, since both waves travel at 343 m/s through the same air and so always arrive together
A quiet spot, since the path difference is 1.5 wavelengths and the waves arrive half a cycle out of phase
A half-loudness spot, since each speaker gives equal intensity and the two sounds simply add incoherently
A loud spot, since the path difference exceeds one wavelength and the waves are therefore back in step

rubric: Wavelength is 0.5 m, so 0.75 m is 1.5 wavelengths, an odd number of half-wavelengths, which gives destructive interference.
Distractors treat any path difference over a wavelength as constructive, ignore phase, or treat coherent sources as incoherent.

items.prompt: A glass lens (n = 1.50) needs a single-layer anti-reflection coating for 550 nm light at normal incidence, with minimal reflection as the aim. Which coating is best?

options.label: n = 1.38, thickness 100 nm
n = 1.38, thickness 50 nm
n = 1.38, thickness 200 nm
n = 1.70, thickness 81 nm

rubric: A quarter-wave layer (550/(4*1.38), about 100 nm) with n below the glass index gives destructive interference of both reflections.
Distractors: 200 nm is a half-wave layer (no cancellation), 1.70 gives no relative inversion so reflection is enhanced, and 50 nm is an eighth-wave.

items.prompt: A diffraction-limited telescope must separate two stars half as far apart as it can now. Atmospheric blur is negligible and the observing wavelength stays the same. Which change best achieves this?

options.label: Double the exposure time at the same aperture
Fit an eyepiece with twice the magnification
Double the diameter of the objective aperture
Double the focal length of the objective

rubric: Angular resolution is about 1.22*lambda/D, so only a larger aperture reduces the minimum resolvable angle.
Longer focal length, higher magnification and longer exposure enlarge or brighten the image without removing the diffraction limit.

items.prompt: An ultrasound scan must image a structure 12 cm deep and resolve features of about 1 mm. Tissue attenuation grows roughly in proportion to frequency, and wavelength in tissue is about 1540/f. Which probe frequency is the best compromise?

options.label: 0.5 MHz, with wavelength near 3 mm, giving deep penetration that matches the depth of the structure
3 MHz, with wavelength near 0.5 mm, fine enough for 1 mm features while attenuation is tolerable at depth
15 MHz, with wavelength near 0.1 mm, giving much finer detail even though signal fades somewhat at depth
40 MHz, with wavelength near 0.04 mm, giving the sharpest resolution since attenuation is only a minor issue

rubric: 3 MHz meets the 1 mm resolution criterion and keeps attenuation workable at 12 cm.
15 and 40 MHz attenuate far too much at this depth; 0.5 MHz has a wavelength too long to resolve 1 mm.

items.prompt: A student must find the wavelength of a red laser (about 630 nm) from a single reading of the first-order maximum on a screen 2.0 m away, with position read to 0.5 mm. The aim is the smallest relative error. Which setup is best?

options.label: A single slit 0.10 mm wide, since its broad central maximum gives the largest and clearest pattern to read
A double slit with 0.05 mm spacing, since fringes spaced about 25 mm apart leave only a small reading error
A double slit with 0.25 mm spacing, since the bright evenly spaced fringes are easy to locate precisely
A 600 lines/mm grating, since the first maximum sits about 0.8 m off-axis and 0.5 mm is then a tiny fraction

rubric: The grating puts the first maximum at a large offset, so a 0.5 mm reading error is a very small relative error (well under 0.1%).
Double-slit fringes are only a few to 25 mm from the center, giving errors of 2% to 10%, and a single slit does not give a clean wavelength measurement this way.

items.prompt: A 50 km link must carry very high bit rates over silica fibre. Judge which fibre is best for keeping pulses distinct, given that cost is secondary.

options.label: Multimode step-index fibre, since its wide core captures more light and so keeps the pulses sharper
Single-mode fibre, since one guided path removes modal dispersion that would smear the pulses at this length
Any silica fibre, since pulse spreading is set by absorption in the glass rather than by path differences
Large-core multimode fibre, since more modes carry bits in parallel and average out any pulse spreading

rubric: Over long distances multimode fibres suffer modal dispersion, which broadens pulses and limits bit rate; single-mode fibre avoids it.
Distractors confuse light capture with pulse sharpness, treat extra modes as helpful, or blame absorption instead of dispersion.

items.prompt: An engineer judges noise-control options for a machine room producing a 100 Hz hum plus hissing at several kHz (sound speed 343 m/s). Which statements are well supported? Select all that apply.

options.label: Active cancellation works equally across the whole room at any frequency, since destructive interference is global
Active cancellation suits the 100 Hz hum, since the long wavelength makes phase alignment within a small fraction of a wavelength easier
A thin foam layer is the best way to absorb the 100 Hz hum, since thin porous layers absorb long wavelengths efficiently
Porous absorbers are effective for the kHz hiss, since a layer of modest thickness is comparable to the short wavelengths

rubric: The 100 Hz wavelength is about 3.4 m, so cancellation tolerates modest phase error; porous absorbers need thickness comparable to a fraction of the wavelength, which is easy only at high frequency.
Distractors assume thin foam works at long wavelengths or that cancellation is uniform in space, which fails because the cancelled zone shrinks with wavelength.

items.prompt: A student builds a spectrometer to resolve the sodium doublet at 589.0 nm and 589.6 nm. The needed resolving power is R = lambda/delta-lambda, about 1000 or more, and a grating gives R = mN, where N is the number of illuminated lines. Which set-up, all in first order, meets the requirement?

options.label: 500 lines/mm, 3 mm of the grating illuminated
1000 lines/mm, 0.5 mm of the grating illuminated
200 lines/mm, 4 mm of the grating illuminated
500 lines/mm, 1 mm of the grating illuminated

rubric: Required R is about 982; 500 lines/mm over 3 mm gives N = 1500 and so R = 1500, which meets it.
The others give R = 500, 800 and 500: line density alone does not set resolving power, the total number of illuminated lines does.

items.prompt: A single quarter-wave layer is to be coated on glass (n = 1.50) in air so that reflection cancels completely at the design wavelength. Judging by the amplitude-matching criterion, which film index is best?
rubric: Complete cancellation needs equal reflected amplitudes at both interfaces, which requires n_film = sqrt(1.50) ≈ 1.22.
1.38 is the common MgF2 choice: it is practical but leaves residual reflection.

items.prompt: A student claims that doubling the slit separation d in a double-slit experiment doubles the fringe spacing on the screen. Which evaluation is correct?

options.label: Wrong: spacing is proportional to 1/d, so doubling d halves it and the pattern becomes finer
Right: spacing doubles, since a larger d increases the angle between orders and spreads the fringes
Wrong: spacing depends only on wavelength and screen distance, so doubling d leaves it unchanged
Right: spacing is proportional to d, so doubling d doubles it because path differences scale with d

rubric: Fringe spacing is λL/d, so it is inversely proportional to d.
Distractors confuse the direct and inverse dependence or ignore d altogether.

items.prompt: To resolve the sodium doublet (589.0 nm and 589.6 nm) you need a resolving power R = λ/Δλ of about 980, where R = mN. Which grating, fully illuminated, meets this?

options.label: 700 lines, first order
900 lines, first order
500 lines, second order
400 lines, second order

rubric: R = mN gives 2 × 500 = 1000, which exceeds 980.
The other options give 800, 700 and 900, which fall short; learners often ignore the order m.

items.prompt: A 50 km optical link must carry 10 Gb/s with minimal pulse broadening. Judging by this criterion, which fibre choice is best?

options.label: Single-mode fibre, because one guided mode removes the modal dispersion that broadens pulses over distance
Multimode step-index fibre, because more modes carry more power and so pulses arrive sharper at the far end
Multimode step-index fibre, because its wide core collects more light and so removes any need for amplifiers
Multimode graded-index fibre, because its index profile eliminates every kind of dispersion over long spans

rubric: Single-mode fibre removes modal dispersion, which dominates at high rates over tens of km.
Graded-index fibre only reduces modal dispersion; extra modes add spread rather than sharpness.

items.prompt: A student says: for sound in air, a source approaching a stationary observer at speed u gives the same frequency as an observer approaching a stationary source at speed u, since only relative motion matters. Evaluate the claim.

options.label: Incorrect: air defines a rest frame, so the cases give f·v/(v−u) and f·(v+u)/v, which differ
Incorrect: the moving-source case gives no shift because wavelength in air is set by the source frequency alone
Correct: both cases give f·v/(v−u) because wavefronts compress equally whichever party moves toward the other
Correct: Doppler shift depends only on relative speed, so both cases give f·(v+u)/v exactly, as in relativity

rubric: Sound needs a medium, so source motion changes wavelength while observer motion changes the rate of wavefront arrival, and the results differ.
The relativity-style symmetry applies to light in vacuum, not to sound.

items.prompt: A telescope is diffraction-limited, and you must separate closer stars, meaning a smaller Rayleigh angle 1.22λ/D. Which changes achieve this? Select all that apply.

options.label: Lengthen the focal length at the same aperture
Observe at a shorter wavelength
Use a larger aperture diameter D
Add an eyepiece with higher magnification

rubric: The Rayleigh angle depends only on λ and D, so a larger D or smaller λ helps.
Magnification and focal length change image scale but not the diffraction limit.

items.prompt: A photographer shoots a calm lake with the sun behind her. Glare reflects off the water at about 53° incidence, near Brewster's angle for water (n = 1.33). She wants to cut this glare with a linear polarising filter. Which orientation best meets the goal?

options.label: Transmission axis at 45°, because this blocks equal parts of both components of the reflected light
Any orientation works equally, because light reflected at any angle from water is unpolarised
Transmission axis horizontal, because the reflected light is mostly polarised vertically, perpendicular to the surface
Transmission axis vertical, because the reflected light is mostly polarised horizontally, parallel to the surface

rubric: Near Brewster's angle the reflected light is polarised parallel to the surface, so a vertical axis blocks it.
Distractors reverse the polarisation direction or deny that reflection polarises light.

items.prompt: Design a Keplerian beam expander using two positive lenses that gives a collimated output with 5× magnification of beam diameter. Which design meets this?

options.label: f1 = +10 cm, f2 = +50 cm, spaced 60 cm
f1 = +10 cm, f2 = +50 cm, spaced 40 cm
f1 = +10 cm, f2 = +50 cm, spaced 50 cm
f1 = +50 cm, f2 = +10 cm, spaced 60 cm

rubric: Collimated output needs a spacing f1 + f2 = 60 cm, and the ratio f2/f1 = 5 sets the expansion.
Wrong spacing leaves the beam converging or diverging; swapping the lenses shrinks the beam.

items.prompt: Design a pipe (speed of sound 343 m/s, ideal ends) whose resonances include 300 Hz and 500 Hz but not 400 Hz. Which pipe meets this?

options.label: Closed at one end, length 1.72 m
Open at both ends, length 0.86 m
Open at both ends, length 1.72 m
Closed at one end, length 0.86 m

rubric: A closed pipe of 0.86 m has f1 ≈ 100 Hz and only odd harmonics: 100, 300, 500 Hz, with no 400 Hz.
Open pipes include all harmonics, so they either include 400 Hz or miss 300 Hz; a closed 1.72 m pipe misses both targets.

items.prompt: A grating spectrometer must record 600–1000 nm in first order without contamination from higher orders. Which fix completes the design?

options.label: Narrow the entrance slit, because this separates overlapping orders in angle and removes the contamination
Add a long-pass filter with cutoff near 1100 nm, because second order from 1200–2000 nm lands at the same angles
Add a long-pass filter with cutoff near 550 nm, because second order from 300–500 nm lands at the same angles as 600–1000 nm
Add a short-pass filter with cutoff near 550 nm, because second order from 300–500 nm lands at the same angles as 600–1000 nm

rubric: Second-order light at λ/2 (300–500 nm) overlaps first-order 600–1000 nm, so a long-pass filter near 550 nm removes it while passing the band.
A short-pass filter would remove the wanted band; slit width changes resolution, not order overlap.

items.prompt: You must rotate linear polarisation by 90° using N ideal polarisers, each turned 90°/N from the previous, so that at least 90% of the intensity is transmitted. Which is the fewest from this list that meets this?

options.label: 30 polarisers
10 polarisers
5 polarisers
20 polarisers

rubric: Transmission is cos^(2N)(90°/N): about 0.60 for 5, 0.78 for 10, 0.88 for 20 and 0.92 for 30.
Only 30 exceeds 90%; learners underestimate how slowly losses fall with N.

items.prompt: Design a single thin-lens system that forms a real, inverted image at magnification −2 on a screen, with object-to-screen distance fixed at 90 cm. Which design meets this?

options.label: f = 30 cm, object 45 cm from the lens
f = 20 cm, object 60 cm from the lens
f = 15 cm, object 30 cm from the lens
f = 20 cm, object 30 cm from the lens

rubric: m = −2 gives s' = 2s, and s + s' = 90 gives s = 30 cm and s' = 60 cm, so f = 20 cm.
The other options give a wrong total distance or a magnification of −1 or −0.5.

items.prompt: A double-slit setup uses λ = 500 nm and a screen at L = 2.0 m. Design requirements: fringe spacing of at least 1.0 mm, and the 5th-order fringe missing because of the single-slit envelope (d = 5a). Which slit separation d and width a meet both? Select all that apply.
rubric: Spacing λL/d = 1e-6/d must be ≥ 1 mm, so d ≤ 1.0 mm, and d = 5a puts the missing order at 5.
The a = 0.25 mm option gives d/a = 2, and d = 2.0 mm gives only 0.5 mm spacing.

items.prompt: An engineer builds a Michelson interferometer to track thermal expansion, using an LED with a coherence length of about 20 µm. The arms differ by roughly 1 mm and no fringes appear. Keeping the LED, which change makes the design work?

options.label: Adjust the arms to be equal in length within about 20 µm, so the path difference is inside the coherence length
Move the screen farther from the beam splitter, so the fringes spread out enough to be seen
Use larger mirrors, so more light returns and the weak 1 mm fringes become visible
Place a narrow slit before the detector, so the spatial filtering restores fringe contrast at 1 mm path difference

rubric: Fringes need a path difference within the source's coherence length, so the arms must be matched to about 20 µm.
Slits, screen distance and mirror size do not restore temporal coherence.
